mixup.belief: Thinks the parts need not be equal to be called halves, thirds or quarters
signs: Cuts a cake into 4 uneven pieces and calls each a quarter

because.rule: shown only to a child the learner model holds this mix-up for, at this beat; any other child gets the script's own board

judge.by: a separate Claude judge (Opus), packet only, p412+l1366
judge.notes: Waves are consistent and correct (parts 4 'Chaar barabar tukde', cut 1/3 'Teen barabar tukde', cut 1/4 'Ek chauthai', parts 3 'Ek tihai'). With marks false the child must judge equal size herself, so a child who cuts uneven pieces is graded off ('PAAS' / 'itna chook'), which shows the unequal-parts mix-up where it goes wrong. The subs state the rule ('Chaar tukde sab ek jaise hone chahiye') but not where to cut, so not counted as giving the answer. Minor, not counted: 'silisila' is a misspelling of 'silsila' and a literary word for class 4; wave 3's sub says 'Chaar tukde' though one cut at 1/4 makes two pieces. Both screens are legible with nothing cut off; the coach line 'Barabar tukde dekho' is low-contrast but readable.

judge2.by: a second separate Claude judge (Opus), packet only
judge2.notes: Every wave's title and sub agree with its item (parts:4 / cut 1/4 with 'chaar', cut 1/3 / parts:3 with 'teen'), and with no cut marks the child must judge equal size herself, so unequal cuts get 'PAAS' / 'itna chook' feedback, which shows a child with the mix-up that uneven pieces are not quarters or thirds. Minor points that are not faults: 'silisila' is a misspelling of 'silsila', the sub 'Chaar tukde sab ek jaise hone chahiye' states the rule rather than letting the child find it, the coach line 'Barabar tukde dekho' is low-contrast but legible, and p360 was not supplied.
